questions.text: In what historical period of Israel did Elimelech sojourn in Moab because of a famine?

options.text: In the days when the judges ruled the land
During the reign of Saul the first king
During the forty years of desert wandering
In the peaceful reign of King Solomon

questions.text: From which city in Judah did Elimelech, his wife Naomi, and their two sons originate?

options.text: From the priestly city of Hebron in the south
From the city of Beth-lehem in the land of Judah
From the tabernacle city of Shiloh in the hills
From the border town of Bethel near the mountains

questions.text: What were the names of the two sons of Elimelech and Naomi who died in the country of Moab?

options.text: Othniel and Kenaz from the southern plain
Gershom and Eliezer from the eastern desert
Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Judah
Phinehas and Hophni from the holy sanctuary

questions.text: What were the names of the two Moabitish women whom Mahlon and Chilion took to wife?

options.text: Orpah and Ruth, women of the country of Moab
Rachel and Leah, the two builders of Israel
Milcah and Tirzah, daughters of Manasseh
Peninnah and Hannah from Mount Ephraim

questions.text: What tidings did Naomi hear in Moab that prompted her to return unto the land of Judah?

options.text: That the kings of Moab were preparing for war
That the LORD had visited his people in giving bread
That her kinsmen in Judah had sent for her with gold
That the sanctuary at Shiloh had been destroyed

questions.text: How did Orpah and Ruth react when Naomi urged them both to return unto their mothers' houses?

options.text: Both daughters-in-law departed at once into Moab
Orpah kissed her mother in law; but Ruth clave unto her
Both daughters-in-law refused to leave Naomi's side
Ruth returned to Moab while Orpah went to Judah

questions.text: With what famous words of devotion did Ruth cling to Naomi on the road to Judah?

options.text: Whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people
I will follow thee only until we reach the border of Jordan
Give me a portion of silver and I will return to my people
The gods of Moab shall ever remain the gods of my fathers

questions.text: What name did Naomi ask the women of Bethlehem to call her upon her sorrowful return?

options.text: Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt bitterly
Call me Deborah, for I have returned in great victory to Judah
Call me Sarah, for I shall yet be a mother of many nations
Call me Hannah, for the LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping

questions.text: At what season of the agricultural year did Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem?

options.text: At the beginning of the early barley harvest
At the solemn feast of the vintage of grapes
In the midst of the cold winter wheat sowing
At the gathering of the summer figs and olives

questions.text: Who was Boaz in Bethlehem unto whose field Ruth came to glean ears of corn?

options.text: A mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech
The chief magistrate and judge of the city of Bethlehem
A wealthy merchant trading in purple cloth from Tyre
The high priest ministering at the tabernacle in Shiloh

questions.text: How did Ruth come to glean specifically in the fruitful field belonging unto Boaz?

options.text: Her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging to Boaz
Naomi sent her directly with a written token to his reapers
The elders of Bethlehem appointed her that portion of land
Boaz had sent his servants to invite her to his harvest

questions.text: With what pious greeting did Boaz address his reapers when he came from Bethlehem?

options.text: The LORD be with you. And they answered: The LORD bless thee
Peace be unto this fruitful field and unto all that labour
Make haste with the sickle, for the summer storm draweth near
May the gods of our fathers grant an abundant harvest of corn

questions.text: What special kindness and provision did Boaz command his young men to grant unto Ruth?

options.text: To let her glean among the sheaves and drop handfuls on purpose
To give her thirty pieces of silver at the end of every day
To load an ass with three full sacks of winnowed wheat
To set apart a permanent field for her own inheritance

questions.text: How much barley did Ruth beat out after gleaning in Boaz's field until eventide?

options.text: Exactly three measures of fine parched wheat
And it was about an ephah of barley beaten out
Ten full measures of coarse unthreshed grain
Only a small handful of dry leftover stalks

questions.explanation: An ephah was an ancient dry measure of capacity equal to approximately 22 litres (about three pecks or half a bushel).

questions.text: How did Naomi identify Boaz when Ruth recounted the kindness she had received from him?

options.text: The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen (redeemers)
He is the chief captain of the armies of the tribe of Judah
He is a stranger from Gilead who hath purchased land in Bethlehem
He is an elder who once dwelt as an exile in the country of Moab

questions.text: What counsel did Naomi give Ruth to seek rest at the threshingfloor of Boaz by night?

options.text: Wash thyself, anoint thee, and lay thee down at his feet
Bring ten loaves of barley bread as an offering to his reapers
Stand at the gate of the floor and call upon him with tears
Wait until daybreak and petition the elders of the city for help

questions.text: At what hour of the night did Boaz awake afraid and discover a woman lying at his feet?

options.text: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was afraid
At the very first cockcrowing before the morning light
At the beginning of the third solemn night watch of guards
Shortly after the sun had gone down behind the western hills

questions.text: What humble plea did Ruth speak when Boaz asked: Who art thou?

options.text: Spread thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman
I am a poor stranger seeking shelter from the cold night air
Deliver me from the hands of the reapers who pursue me unjustly
Give me a measure of barley that I may return to my mother's home

questions.text: What noble character testimony did Boaz pronounce concerning Ruth before all the people?

options.text: All the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman
Thou art known as the most skillful handmaid in all Bethlehem
Thy wisdom in speech exceedeth all the daughters of the Moabites
Thou hast brought great riches and renown unto the house of Judah

questions.text: What legal impediment did Boaz mention before he could perform the part of a kinsman?

options.text: Howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I in the line of redemption
He had not yet accumulated sufficient silver to buy the field
The elders of Bethlehem had forbidden marriage with foreign women
The land of Elimelech had already been pledged unto another man

questions.text: With what parting gift of grain did Boaz send Ruth home unto Naomi before morning light?

options.text: He measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her
Ten full measures of wheat carried in earthen vessels
Two small sheaves of freshly gathered summer barley
A single sack of winnowed corn laden upon an ass

questions.text: Where in Bethlehem did Boaz sit down to resolve the matter of the inheritance of Elimelech?

options.text: Then went Boaz up to the gate, and sat him down there
In the inner court of the local synagogue of elders
Upon the threshingfloor where the barley was winnowed
Before the entrance of his own spacious dwelling house

questions.text: How many elders of the city of Bethlehem did Boaz summon as official witnesses?

options.text: And he took ten men of the elders of the city as witnesses
Twelve men representing the twelve tribes of Israel
Seventy elders chosen from among all the families of Judah
Three judges presiding over the judicial court of Bethlehem

questions.text: Why did the nearer kinsman refuse to redeem the parcel of land belonging to Naomi?

options.text: I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance
Because he lacked the necessary silver to purchase the field
Because he refused to enter into any transaction before the elders
Because the land of Elimelech was barren and without living water

questions.text: What symbolic legal custom was performed in Israel to confirm the transfer of redemption?

options.text: A man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour
They broke an earthen flagon before the elders of the gate
They struck hands together and sealed the covenant in blood
They cast a silver shekel into a vessel of consecrated oil

questions.explanation: Plucking off and delivering the shoe symbolized the renunciation of one's legal right to the land and confirmed the transfer of redemption unto another.

questions.text: With what ancient blessing did the elders and people at the gate bless Ruth?

options.text: The LORD make the woman like Rachel and like Leah, who built Israel
May she bear ten sons to be mighty captains of war in Judah
May her inheritance extend from the river Jordan unto the great sea
May she be renowned as Deborah who judged Israel under the palm

questions.text: What was the name of the son born unto Ruth and Boaz, whom Naomi laid in her bosom?

options.text: Jesse, the father of King David
David, the future anointed king
And they called his name Obed
Pharez, the ancient tribal head

questions.text: Which supreme king of Israel descended from Obed according to the close of the book of Ruth?

options.text: And Jesse begat David, the king of Israel
Solomon, who built the glorious temple of God
Saul, who was chosen from the tribe of Benjamin
Hezekiah, who walked faithfully before the LORD

questions.text: With which ancestor of the tribe of Judah does the genealogy at the end of Ruth begin?

options.text: Now these are the generations of Pharez (son of Judah)
Nahshon, the prince of the children of Judah in the desert
Boaz, the noble kinsman redeemer of Bethlehem
Elimelech, the father of Mahlon and Chilion in Moab

questions.text: Who said unto Naomi: "Whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people"?

options.text: Hannah
Ruth
Rahab
Orpah

questions.text: What were the names of the two daughters-in-law of Naomi according to Ruth 1:4?

options.text: Michal
Hannah
Ruth
Orpah
